label: Spacecraft cabin
description: Sea-level air at 14.7 psia with 21% oxygen, ventilated at roughly 20 cm/s. Everything that burns here is solid: fabrics, plastics, insulation, cable jackets.
assumption: Ventilation speed is a design value, not a measured ISS number.

label: Surface habitat
description: NASA's exploration atmosphere: 8.2 psia with about 34% oxygen. The challenge statement allows 30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psia or less, so this sits inside that window. Solid materials dominate, as in the cabin.
assumption: The same atmosphere is used for both Moon and Mars; the two were merged into one environment.

label: Space suit
description: Pure oxygen at 4.3 psia. The highest oxygen concentration and the lowest pressure of the four environments, which makes almost any material flammable. Ventilation is weak compared with a cabin.
assumption: Airflow is an estimate; suits have little forced circulation.

label: Rover / vehicle
description: Same exploration atmosphere as the habitat, but a pressurized rover also carries liquid fuel lines. That is why liquid fuels matter here while fabrics and plastics matter in the cabin.
assumption: Airflow is higher because a vehicle moves air for cooling; this is a reasoned estimate, not a published figure.
